title: CMU 2026 Commencement: Jensen Huang on resilience, the AI reset, and putting your heart in the work
summary: Jensen tells his immigrant origin story and the near-death Sega episode at Nvidia, framing failure as character-building and the CEO role as responsibility. He then argues AI is a full reset of computing and a once-in-a-generation infrastructure buildout, and that everyone should engage with it optimistically and responsibly.

principles.text: Being CEO is responsibility for keeping the company alive, not power.
principles.quote: I learned early that being CEO is not about power, but the responsibility that comes with keeping the company alive.

principles.text: Honesty and humility can be met with generosity, even in business.
principles.quote: And that honesty and humility can be met with generosity and kindness, even in business.

principles.text: Failure is not the opposite of success; it builds humility, character and resilience.
principles.quote: we learn never to see failure as the opposite of success. Each failure is just another learning moment, a humility moment, a character-strengthening moment.

principles.text: Desperation can force invention; a crisis reset produced methods Nvidia still uses.
principles.quote: We used the money to reset the company. And out of desperation, we invented new ways of designing chips and computers that we still use today.

principles.text: Optimism helps you start hard things; reality shows they're harder, and you reinvent anyway.
principles.quote: For 33 years, Nvidia had reinvented itself over and over again, each time asking, "How hard can it be?" And each time learning, "It's harder than we thought."

principles.text: AI amplifies human capability; the risk is being outpaced by people who use AI better.
principles.quote: AI is not likely to replace you. But someone using AI better than you might.
